items.followUp: Differentiate between active transport and diffusion.

rubric.why: Identifies osmosis as the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that osmosis involves water molecules moving through a selectively permeable membrane.

rubric.why: Identifies diffusion as movement down a concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that diffusion moves particles from a higher to a lower concentration.

modelAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration.
Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.

items.followUp: Differentiate between benign and malignant growths in terms of their spread.

rubric.why: Identifies malignant tumors as cancerous and describes their invasive or spreading behaviour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that malignant tumors are cancerous and invade nearby tissues or spread to other parts of the body.

rubric.why: Distinguishes benign tumors by their noncancerous, localized nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that benign tumors are noncancerous and remain localized.

modelAnswer: Malignant tumors are cancerous; they invade surrounding tissues and may spread to other parts of the body.
Benign tumors are noncancerous and remain localized; they do not invade or spread to other parts of the body.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a cofactor and a coenzyme.

rubric.why: Gives the defining tight association of a prosthetic group with its enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a prosthetic group is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.

rubric.why: Distinguishes coenzymes as organic cofactors that associate loosely or temporarily with enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a coenzyme is an organic cofactor that binds loosely or temporarily to an enzyme.

modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component that is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
A coenzyme is an organic cofactor that is loosely or temporarily bound to an enzyme.

items.followUp: Describe what happens to the enzyme and substrate after an enzyme-substrate complex forms.

rubric.why: Identifies the substrate binding at the enzyme's active site as the first step in complex formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the substrate fits into or binds to the enzyme's active site.

rubric.why: Names the structure formed when the substrate binds to the enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that this binding forms an enzyme-substrate (ES) complex.

modelAnswer: The substrate fits into the enzyme’s specific active site and binds there.
This binding forms an enzyme-substrate (ES) complex.
